rationale: A wins because it keeps the story inside the supplied facts and makes the strongest live hook cleanly: "It has not said how often they get it wrong." B is useful, but it keeps writing checks the update cannot cash, especially "bets the company on agents" and the competitor dressing around "Notion, Smartsheet and Monday." The gap is not polish; it is discipline.
gaps_in_A: "Pricing is not finalized, so there is nothing to report yet" throws away a risky but real SaaS business-model angle. There may be a story if a pricing lead will discuss what unit Airtable is considering charging for.

"whether an agent platform is the growth argument investors want to hear" is a soft valuation thesis without revenue, growth, a current mark, or an investor on record. A admits the peg is soft, but the angle still needs a harder anchor.
"Next step: journalist-fit-check once you pick one angle" punts the strategic call. It should tell the founder which angle to lead with and which ones to park until proof exists.
gaps_in_B: "bets the company on agents" overstates the facts. The update says repositioning and launch, not existential company bet.
"established category leader" and "Airtable, Notion, Smartsheet and Monday" are unsupported by the update. That's beat-color cosplay unless the model has evidence.
"Nobody has settled on what an AI agent should cost" is too broad for one company's unfinalized pricing. Make it "Airtable has not settled" or bring proof that the category is stuck.
"Airtable shipping agents with pricing unfinalized is a usable data point" is only usable if Airtable will talk on record. Otherwise it is an absence dressed as a trend piece.
